data.text: Should we add a gate after code change in this project (configurable per project, with a global generic gate) that right before merge, even a forced one, the agent checks the pre-commit gates on the modified files and tests, corrects the issues it finds, and then proceeds with the merge? Answers: (1) check ALWAYS runs, also on forced merges/completes, NOT skippable by --force; failure refuses the merge; only an explicit operator override via the approval route passes it. (2) FIX AND COMMIT: fixable issues fixed by hooks on the item's OWN changed files only, committed to the item's branch as a normal commit, touched files listed, then the check re-runs; never touch or re-stage files outside the lease. (3) SCOPE: the project's pre-commit hooks on the item's changed files plus the item's changed/added test files executed, not the whole suite.

data.alternatives: Skippable by --force: rejected, the forced merges are the ones that most need the check. Report only, no fix: rejected, agents then repeat the same format failures. Run the whole suite: rejected, that is the ci gate.
data.consequences: A merge can take the hook time of the changed files (budget knob); a project with no hooks gets the generic set; a hook that cannot run is visible as unavailable; the operator override is the only way past a failing check. Absorbs DX-autoformat-on-commit (and its lease-scope amendment).
data.context: Main went red from merges that skipped format and lint checks; the merge smoke gate covers a fixed set (import probe, ruff, bandit, changed tests) and the ci gate runs the pre-push stage only after the work is done, and a forced merge skips both. The operator wants merged code always checked by the project's own hooks, with the agent correcting what it finds.
data.decision: Right before a merge lands, ddflow runs the project's pre-commit hooks on the files the item changed, and executes the item's changed or added test files (never the whole suite). (1) It ALWAYS runs: also on a forced merge and a forced complete. --force does not skip it. A failure refuses the merge; only an explicit operator override recorded through the approval route passes it. (2) Fix and commit: issues a hook can fix itself (formatting, import order, trailing whitespace) are fixed on the item's OWN changed files only and committed to the item's branch as a normal commit; the touched files are listed; then the check re-runs. It never touches a file outside the item and never re-stages a file outside the lease. (3) Scope: the project's .pre-commit-config.yaml hooks restricted to the changed files (pre-commit run --files), falling back to a generic default set when the project has no pre-commit config. A hook whose tool is missing or cannot run is recorded unavailable, never passed; what an unavailable hook does is a [premerge] knob. It is configurable per project in a [premerge] section with a generic global default, works in worktrees and lanes, uses no network and never installs a tool.
data.title: Pre-merge pre-commit gate: the project's hooks on the item's changed files always run before a merge, fixes are committed, force does not skip it

data.body: Governed by D-premerge-precommit-gate-2026-11-12. SIZE M. WHAT: a service (ddflow/services/premerge.py) plus a [premerge] config section, and a verb 'ddflow premerge [ITEM]' that works on the item's worktree: (1) the item's changed files = the three-dot diff of its branch against its base (own changes only, never files a merge pulled in; reuse services/ci/ruff.changed_python's own mode and services/ci/ruff._safe_files); (2) project hooks: .pre-commit-config.yaml hooks of the stages in [premerge].stages (default pre-commit) run via 'pre-commit run --files <changed> --hook-stage <stage>', the test-running hooks of the pre-push stage left off exactly as services/ci/shell.py leaves them; no pre-commit config: the generic default set (trailing whitespace, final newline, merge-conflict markers, private-key header, large file, and ruff check+format for Python through the [ci] ruff_bin) as built-in checks; (3) FIX MODE: a hook that modifies a file makes pre-commit exit 1; compare snapshots (as ci/ruff.auto_fix does), keep only changes inside the item's changed set, restore anything a hook touched outside it (never re-stage outside the lease), commit the rest with 'git commit' as 'premerge: apply hook fixes' naming the files, then re-run the hooks once in check mode; (4) the item's changed or added test files are executed ([premerge].test_command, appended with the files; none: skipped, not passed); (5) per-hook results: passed, failed, fixed, unavailable (tool missing, hook repo not cached and no network, budget spent), skipped; a missing tool is NEVER passed and no tool is installed; (6) [premerge] knobs: enabled, stages, budget_s, on_unavailable (unavailable|refuse, default per the smoke gate: unavailable), fix (default true), commit_fixes, test_command, skip_hooks, max_fix_rounds (default 1; bounded), generic_hooks; each with a doc, check, and strictest/tighten-only value; knob manifests under templates/upgrade/unreleased. No network, no installs, runs in worktrees and lanes (cwd = the item's tree, the lease's globs untouched). Output lists the touched files and each hook's result; outcome passed|failed|unavailable. ACCEPTANCE and FALSIFIERS (tests first, each must fail on the unfixed code): (a) a branch with an unformatted changed file ends fixed, committed, touched file listed, re-check passed; (b) a file outside the item that is unformatted is byte-identical after and absent from the commit and from the index; (c) a missing hook tool (PATH without pre-commit, or ruff) gives unavailable, never passed, other hooks still run; (d) a project without .pre-commit-config.yaml gets the generic set; (e) the changed test file runs and a failing one fails; (f) budget exhaustion is unavailable; (g) max_fix_rounds bounds the loop (a hook that always rewrites ends failed, not looping). Independent of GM-smoke-gate: it shares no file and does not import smoke; unify the Check/Report types in the enforce slice. Docs: help topic, knob register entries (README row and default.toml entries land with the docs slice, GM-premerge-docs, if those files are leased).
data.title: Pre-merge pre-commit gate, slice 1: ddflow premerge runs the project's hooks on the item's changed files, fixes and commits them, runs the changed tests

data.body: Governed by D-premerge-precommit-gate-2026-11-12. SIZE S-M. WHAT: ddflow merge calls services/premerge on the item's tree right after the smoke gate (GM-smoke-enforce) and before any git landing, in the place _gate_blockers sits (a refusal that --force does not lift, like the failed-review blockers); fix mode commits the item's own fixes first, then the check result decides. A failed check refuses the merge naming the hook and files. unavailable follows [premerge].on_unavailable. The same check runs on 'complete' for an item whose merge did not run it (a merge landed by hand, a PR-mode merge) as a blocker not lifted by --force. PR-mode and merge-queue landings run it too (the queue per member before the batch suite, BG-ci). Unify the Check/Report types with services/smoke.py (one shared result type). Add the 'ddflow premerge' declared command and MCP family entry. ACCEPTANCE and FALSIFIERS: merge --force of a branch with an unformatted changed file ends fixed and committed (the landed tree is formatted), a branch with a hook failure no hook can fix is refused even with --force (and an agent's --force is refused as before); no ci run record exists for a refused merge; a missing tool is unavailable and does not refuse by default; [premerge].enabled = false restores today's behaviour only through the operator's config (an agent cannot turn it off; strictest value is on). Tests first.
data.title: Enforce the pre-merge pre-commit gate at merge and complete: not skippable by --force, runs after smoke and before the landing

data.body: Governed by D-premerge-precommit-gate-2026-11-12. SIZE S. WHAT: the only way past a failing pre-merge check: an approval (verb premerge.override) bound to the item, the failing hook ids and a digest of the failing output, requested with '--approval request', answered by the operator in chat, spent after the landing landed (as merge_force.spend does). A person's --force never skips the check; a person overrides with 'ddflow merge ITEM --override-premerge --reason ...' recorded as an override event (listed by 'ddflow gate overrides'). FALSIFIERS: an agent's --force alone is refused; an approval for other hooks is refused; an expired or spent approval is refused; the override is recorded with the failing hooks and the reason. Tests first.
data.title: Operator override of a failing pre-merge check through the approval route, recorded and bound to the exact failing hooks

chunk_findings.detail: The intent for this gate explicitly requires a `[premerge].commit_fixes` knob with a manifest, but the new `PremergeConfig` has no `commit_fixes` field and the change contains no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`. With `fix` defaulting to true, there is no supported way to apply hook fixes without committing them, so a user/operator cannot configure the required behavior (for example, `fix = true`, `commit_fixes = false`); this violates the specified knob set for D-premerge-precommit-gate-2026-11-12.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:PremergeConfig

chunk_findings.detail: The `_COULD_NOT_RUN` substring check (`"An error has occurred" in text`) matches against the full combined stdout+stderr of the pre-commit process, which includes every hook's own diagnostic output. A hook whose error message contains the phrase "An error has occurred" (a common phrasing in Python tooling, e.g. `TypeError: An error has occurred during …`) causes the entire stage to be classified UNAVAILABLE and the function returns early, discarding all individually-parsed hook results for that stage. The run's actual FAILED hooks are lost and the outcome shifts from FAILED to UNAVAILABLE, which under the default `on_unavailable = "unavailable"` misreports a real code problem as a tooling problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/premerge.py:_precommit_round (lines 127-134)

chunk_findings.detail: `path.read_bytes()` and `path.write_bytes(new)` are called without exception handling. The `run` docstring explicitly promises "Never raises for a step's own trouble: that is the step's unavailable," but a `PermissionError` (read-only file system, file owned by another user) or `FileNotFoundError` (file removed between the `p.is_file()` check in `changed_files` and the read here) propagates uncaught through `_generic` → `_hooks_step` → `run`, crashing the verb with a traceback instead of returning a `Report` with the step marked UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/premerge.py:_generic (lines 155-162)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a new `[premerge]` section, and the stated intent lists `commit_fixes` as one of its knobs requiring a knob manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`. The manifest for the change contains knob manifests for `enabled`, `stages`, `budget_s`, `on_unavailable`, `fix`, `test_command`, `skip_hooks`, `max_fix_rounds`, and `generic_hooks`, but no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`. Given an upgrade generated from these manifests, the `premerge.commit_fixes` knob is not recorded with its default and impact, so the change violates its own requirement that each `[premerge]` knob have a manifest.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml (missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The change manifest says these are the new files in the change, and it includes knob-added manifests for the new `[premerge]` knobs, but there is no manifest for `commit_fixes` even though the stated intent requires a knob manifest for each `[premerge]` knob including `commit_fixes`. For an upgrade that reports newly added knobs, `premerge.commit_fixes` will be missing from the upgrade/template set, violating the required per-knob manifest requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml

chunk_findings.detail: The module-level `pytestmark` skips the entire test file whenever `pre-commit` is not installed. That directly prevents the acceptance falsifiers for “a missing hook tool (PATH without pre-commit, or ruff) gives unavailable, never passed” and “a project without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` gets the generic set” from ever failing on unfixed code in an environment without `pre-commit`. For example, on a machine with no `pre-commit` binary, all premerge gate tests are skipped, including `test_a_missing_hook_tool_is_unavailable_never_passed` and the generic-set tests, even though the intent says missing tools should be reported as unavailable rather than causing the gate tests to be absent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that the per-hook result named `tests` is `PM.FAILED`; it never asserts the overall gate outcome is `PM.FAILED`. A service implementation that records the failing test result but computes the overall outcome as `PM.PASSED` (or `PM.UNAVAILABLE`) would still pass this test. Given the intent says the outcome is `passed|failed|unavailable` and acceptance (e) requires a failing changed test file to fail the gate, this test is not a valid falsifier for the overall outcome.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:test_the_changed_test_files_run_and_a_failing_one_fails

chunk_findings.detail: The `[premerge]` config contract is missing the required `commit_fixes` knob. The stated intent lists `commit_fixes` as a required `[premerge]` knob with a doc, check/strictest value, and a `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml` manifest, but neither `PremergeConfig` nor the new knob manifests contain it. As written, an operator cannot separate “apply/report hook fixes” from “commit those fixes”: the only related knob is `fix`, so disabling fixes also disables the fix-reporting behavior, while enabling fixes implies the commit behavior. If the service later reads `cfg.commit_fixes`, this config section will also make it fail with an attribute error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:38 (PremergeConfig.fix)

chunk_findings.detail: The gate can be weakened by knobs that are not tighten-only. `stages` accepts any list, including `[]`, and `generic_hooks` is a plain bool with no strictest/tighten-only constraint. For a project with a `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, setting `stages = []` makes the hook phase run zero stages; for a project without one, setting `generic_hooks = false` makes the hook phase run no generic checks. With no failed or unavailable hook result, and no changed test file to run, the report can still be reported as `passed`, so the premerge gate can be bypassed by config changes that should be refused or tightened by the decision.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:23 (PremergeConfig.stages) and ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:55 (PremergeConfig.generic_hooks)

chunk_findings.detail: The change contract lists `commit_fixes` as a `[premerge]` knob requiring a manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`, but the full manifest list for this change contains no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`. Upgrade tooling or generated upgrade notes will therefore omit this knob, and if the config section defines `premerge.commit_fixes`, the required manifest is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml (missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The module-level `pytestmark` skips the entire test file whenever `pre-commit` is not on `PATH`. This also skips tests that do not need the real `pre-commit` tool, such as `test_no_config_runs_the_generic_set`, `test_generic_set_refuses_markers_and_private_keys`, `test_generic_set_refuses_an_oversized_file`, `test_generic_hooks_off_leaves_a_project_without_config_with_no_hook_step`, and `test_disabled_runs_nothing`. In a unit-test CI environment without the optional `pre-commit` executable, the whole premerge-gate suite is skipped, so regressions in the generic fallback, disabled handling, or budget handling can merge without any failing test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The `STRIP` hook uses GNU-style `sed -i 's/[ \t]*$//'`. On BSD/macOS `sed`, `-i` requires a backup suffix, so the hook exits with an error instead of stripping trailing whitespace. If `pre-commit` is installed on macOS, the module skip is satisfied, but `test_an_unformatted_changed_file_is_fixed_and_committed` fails because `a.txt` is never fixed and the assertions on `rep.fixed`, the fixed file contents, and the generated commit cannot hold. The same assumption appears in the `wide` hook used by `test_a_file_outside_the_item_is_never_touched_or_committed`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:27

chunk_findings.detail: The test builds `test_command` as `f"{sys.executable} -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider"` without quoting the executable path. If the Python executable path contains spaces, for example `C:\Program Files\Python39\python.exe`, the command string parsed by the service is split into `C:\Program` as the program and the rest as arguments, so pytest is never run and the test fails regardless of the premerge implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:test_the_changed_test_files_run_and_a_failing_one_fails

chunk_findings.detail: The stated `[premerge]` knobs include `commit_fixes`, and the intent requires each knob to have a manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`. The change manifest lists all added files and includes manifests for `fix`, `test_command`, `max_fix_rounds`, etc., but no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`; therefore the required registration/manifest artifact for the `commit_fixes` knob is missing.

chunk_findings.detail: `path.read_bytes()` and `path.write_bytes(new)` are called without exception handling. The `run` docstring explicitly promises "Never raises for a step's own trouble: that is the step's unavailable," but a `PermissionError` (read-only file system, file owned by another user) or `FileNotFoundError` (file removed between the `p.is_file()` check in `changed_files` and the read here) propagates uncaught through `_generic` → `_hooks_step` → `run`, crashing the verb with a traceback instead of returning a `Report` with the step marked UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/premerge.py:_generic (lines 155-162)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a new `[premerge]` section, and the stated intent lists `commit_fixes` as one of its knobs requiring a knob manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`. The manifest for the change contains knob manifests for `enabled`, `stages`, `budget_s`, `on_unavailable`, `fix`, `test_command`, `skip_hooks`, `max_fix_rounds`, and `generic_hooks`, but no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`. Given an upgrade generated from these manifests, the `premerge.commit_fixes` knob is not recorded with its default and impact, so the change violates its own requirement that each `[premerge]` knob have a manifest.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml (missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The change manifest says these are the new files in the change, and it includes knob-added manifests for the new `[premerge]` knobs, but there is no manifest for `commit_fixes` even though the stated intent requires a knob manifest for each `[premerge]` knob including `commit_fixes`. For an upgrade that reports newly added knobs, `premerge.commit_fixes` will be missing from the upgrade/template set, violating the required per-knob manifest requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml

chunk_findings.detail: The module-level `pytestmark` skips the entire test file whenever `pre-commit` is not installed. That directly prevents the acceptance falsifiers for “a missing hook tool (PATH without pre-commit, or ruff) gives unavailable, never passed” and “a project without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` gets the generic set” from ever failing on unfixed code in an environment without `pre-commit`. For example, on a machine with no `pre-commit` binary, all premerge gate tests are skipped, including `test_a_missing_hook_tool_is_unavailable_never_passed` and the generic-set tests, even though the intent says missing tools should be reported as unavailable rather than causing the gate tests to be absent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that the per-hook result named `tests` is `PM.FAILED`; it never asserts the overall gate outcome is `PM.FAILED`. A service implementation that records the failing test result but computes the overall outcome as `PM.PASSED` (or `PM.UNAVAILABLE`) would still pass this test. Given the intent says the outcome is `passed|failed|unavailable` and acceptance (e) requires a failing changed test file to fail the gate, this test is not a valid falsifier for the overall outcome.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:test_the_changed_test_files_run_and_a_failing_one_fails

chunk_findings.detail: The new `could_not = not found and any(m in text for m in _COULD_NOT_RUN)` only treats pre-commit’s own “An error has occurred” output as unavailable when no hook line was parsed. If a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has two hooks, the first cached hook can run and print its result line (e.g. `...Passed`), then a later hook’s repo may be uncached with no network; pre-commit prints its own “An error has occurred” and exits 1. Because `found` is non-empty, `could_not` is false, so the function returns only the first hook’s result and records no unavailable result for the second hook. With no failing tests, the gate can be reported as passed even though a hook was unavailable, violating “missing tool/repo unavailable” and “never passed.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/premerge.py:192 (_precommit_round)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `STRIP_PY` is a normal triple-quoted string, so the escapes in the embedded hook source are processed when `STRIP_PY` is assigned. In particular, `rb"[ \t]+(?=\r?\n|\Z)"` contains `\n`, which becomes an actual newline inside the generated `strip.py`’s single-quoted bytes literal, making the hook script syntactically invalid (EOL while scanning string literal). When `test_an_unformatted_changed_file_is_fixed_and_committed` runs, pre-commit executes `python strip.py a.txt`; the hook dies with a `SyntaxError`, so the changed file is not fixed/committed and the test’s “clean status / touched file” assertions fail (or the gate reports failed/unavailable). The embedded source should be raw or the backslashes should be doubled.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:STRIP_PY

evidence.diff_source: delta review of 3 commits since ccebd1c2ff

chunk_findings.detail: The `[premerge]` config contract is missing the required `commit_fixes` knob. The stated intent lists `commit_fixes` as a required `[premerge]` knob with a doc, check/strictest value, and a `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml` manifest, but neither `PremergeConfig` nor the new knob manifests contain it. As written, an operator cannot separate “apply/report hook fixes” from “commit those fixes”: the only related knob is `fix`, so disabling fixes also disables the fix-reporting behavior, while enabling fixes implies the commit behavior. If the service later reads `cfg.commit_fixes`, this config section will also make it fail with an attribute error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:38 (PremergeConfig.fix)

chunk_findings.detail: The gate can be weakened by knobs that are not tighten-only. `stages` accepts any list, including `[]`, and `generic_hooks` is a plain bool with no strictest/tighten-only constraint. For a project with a `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, setting `stages = []` makes the hook phase run zero stages; for a project without one, setting `generic_hooks = false` makes the hook phase run no generic checks. With no failed or unavailable hook result, and no changed test file to run, the report can still be reported as `passed`, so the premerge gate can be bypassed by config changes that should be refused or tightened by the decision.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:23 (PremergeConfig.stages) and ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:55 (PremergeConfig.generic_hooks)

chunk_findings.detail: The change contract lists `commit_fixes` as a `[premerge]` knob requiring a manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`, but the full manifest list for this change contains no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`. Upgrade tooling or generated upgrade notes will therefore omit this knob, and if the config section defines `premerge.commit_fixes`, the required manifest is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml (missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The module-level `pytestmark` skips the entire test file whenever `pre-commit` is not on `PATH`. This also skips tests that do not need the real `pre-commit` tool, such as `test_no_config_runs_the_generic_set`, `test_generic_set_refuses_markers_and_private_keys`, `test_generic_set_refuses_an_oversized_file`, `test_generic_hooks_off_leaves_a_project_without_config_with_no_hook_step`, and `test_disabled_runs_nothing`. In a unit-test CI environment without the optional `pre-commit` executable, the whole premerge-gate suite is skipped, so regressions in the generic fallback, disabled handling, or budget handling can merge without any failing test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: The `STRIP` hook uses GNU-style `sed -i 's/[ \t]*$//'`. On BSD/macOS `sed`, `-i` requires a backup suffix, so the hook exits with an error instead of stripping trailing whitespace. If `pre-commit` is installed on macOS, the module skip is satisfied, but `test_an_unformatted_changed_file_is_fixed_and_committed` fails because `a.txt` is never fixed and the assertions on `rep.fixed`, the fixed file contents, and the generated commit cannot hold. The same assumption appears in the `wide` hook used by `test_a_file_outside_the_item_is_never_touched_or_committed`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:27

chunk_findings.detail: The test builds `test_command` as `f"{sys.executable} -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider"` without quoting the executable path. If the Python executable path contains spaces, for example `C:\Program Files\Python39\python.exe`, the command string parsed by the service is split into `C:\Program` as the program and the rest as arguments, so pytest is never run and the test fails regardless of the premerge implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:test_the_changed_test_files_run_and_a_failing_one_fails

chunk_findings.detail: The stated `[premerge]` knobs include `commit_fixes`, and the intent requires each knob to have a manifest under `templates/upgrade/unreleased`. The change manifest lists all added files and includes manifests for `fix`, `test_command`, `max_fix_rounds`, etc., but no `knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml`; therefore the required registration/manifest artifact for the `commit_fixes` knob is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.premerge.commit_fixes.toml:1

chunk_findings.detail: The new `commit_fixes` knob is not constrained as tighten-only/operator-only, so a project can set `[premerge] commit_fixes = false` while leaving `fix` at its default `true`. In that case, an unformatted changed file is fixed only in the worktree; the hook re-run can report the hook step as fixed/passed, but the item’s branch still contains the unformatted file because no commit was made. This gives a project-settable way to weaken the pre-merge gate’s guarantee that hook fixes are actually committed to the branch, contrary to the stated requirement that each `[premerge]` knob have a strictest/tighten-only value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/premerge.py:50 (`commit_fixes`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `could_not = not found and any(...)` disables the unavailable-hook detection whenever any pre-commit hook line is present. Given a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with two hooks where the first passes and the second is unavailable (missing tool or hook repo not cached/no network), `pre-commit run --files ...` can emit a hook line for the first hook and then a failure for the second, exiting 1. Because `found` is non-empty, `could_not` is false, so the function cannot produce an `UNAVAILABLE` result: if the unavailable hook is represented as a `Failed` hook line, it is recorded as `FAILED`, not `UNAVAILABLE`; if it is represented only by pre-commit’s own failure phrase after a passed hook line, it is omitted entirely and the report can be `passed` from the first hook. This violates the contract that a missing/unavailable hook is reported as unavailable and is never passed while other hooks still run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/premerge.py:_precommit_round

chunk_findings.detail: The added tests that require the real `pre-commit` executable are not decorated with `needs_precommit` (the first added test at line 250 uses a project `.pre-commit-config.yaml` hook, and `test_fix_without_commit_leaves_the_fix_in_the_tree_uncommitted` at line 277 uses the `STRIP` pre-commit hook). The previous triage claimed the whole-file skip had been replaced by per-test `needs_precommit` markers, but these new real-`pre-commit` tests carry none. In a CI lane where the optional `pre-commit` executable is absent, they execute rather than skip; the premerge service reports the hook phase as `UNAVAILABLE`, so the assertions expecting `PM.FAILED` and `rep.fixed == ["a.txt"]` fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_premerge_gate.py:test_a_hook_that_prints_the_could_not_run_phrase_still_fails_as_a_hook
